name: riso-print
title: Riso Print
description: Print a subject in two risograph inks, with the accent plate sliding in off-register and settling a hair out of alignment over grainy paper. A built-in geometric poster stands in for the subject; a host replaces the contents of both .rp-subject layers with its own picture.
useWhen: A title card, poster or logo should arrive as if it came off a two-color risograph, with visible misregistration and ink speckle.
The brand has two inks and the scene should read as a zine, flyer or gig poster rather than a screen.
You want the print to keep a little life after it lands: the accent plate keeps a small stop-motion wobble.
avoidWhen: An existing live scene, photo or video should be re-screened as a printed page for its whole duration: use halftone-print.
The print should pulse to music and swap its ink pair on every beat: use duotone-beat.
Only one element should feel hand-placed on paper while the rest stays clean: use paper-wobble.
author: Remocn
